analysis.investment_thesis: Anupam Rasayan commands a P/E of 85x on earnings that are DECLINING — net profit fell from INR 217 Cr (FY23) to INR 160 Cr (FY25) while revenue also shrank — making the PEG ratio effectively infinite on trailing numbers. With ROE at a shocking 3.3% and free cash flow consistently deeply negative, this is a company destroying capital while priced for perfection.
key_strengths: Long-term revenue CAGR of 19% (2019-2025) reflects a real business with legitimate specialty chemical export relationships
Promoter holding at 59% and long-term customer contracts in agrochemicals/pharma provide some stability to the order book
Significant capex (CWIP peaked at INR 609 Cr in FY24) represents capacity that could eventually drive a revenue inflection
key_risks: Revenue peaked at INR 1,602 Cr in FY23 and has contracted for two consecutive years to INR 1,437 Cr — Chinese competition and agrochemical pricing pressure are structural, not cyclical
Finance costs surging at 29% CAGR while profits fall — INR 112 Cr in interest expense against INR 160 Cr net profit means 70% of earnings service debt
Free cash flow has been negative in 5 of 6 years, consuming INR 440 Cr in FY25 alone — the business requires constant external capital to sustain itself
red_flags: ROE of 3.32% on a INR 3,197 Cr equity base is catastrophically poor — the company is earning less than a fixed deposit on its shareholders' capital
P/E of 85x on DECLINING earnings — PEG is undefined (negative growth). Forward P/E of 58.74x implies the market is paying for a recovery that hasn't appeared in the data
Total debt grew from INR 836 Cr (FY22) to INR 1,382 Cr (FY25) while profits shrank — this is a leveraged bet on a recovery that keeps getting delayed
analysis.detailed_analysis: I have a simple rule: never pay 85 times earnings for a shrinking business. Anupam Rasayan has all three of my worst signals at once — declining revenue, declining profits, and negative free cash flow — packaged in an 'expensive growth stock' valuation. The specialty chemicals sector sounded wonderful two years ago; India supplanting China as a chemical supplier was a compelling thesis. But the data shows the opposite: Chinese manufacturers are winning on cost, and Anupam's customers are walking back orders. The ROE of 3.3% is the most damning single number here — it means that for every INR 100 of equity capital, this company earns INR 3.32. You can do better at a post office. Until revenue inflects back above INR 1,600 Cr, ROE crosses 10%, and FCF turns positive, this stock is uninvestable at any price above 20x earnings — let alone 85x.
